conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have three children - Alex who's 7, Blake who's 20, and Charlie who's also 7.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You have three children: Alex (7), Blake (20), and Charlie (7).

Let me ask you some questions to assess eligibility for each child.

**First, do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand more about Blake, who is 20 years old.

**Is Blake currently in approved education or training?**

(For context: Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training, but normally stops at age 20)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any education or training. He's actually working full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now let me ask about Alex and Charlie, who are both 7 years old.

**Do Alex and Charlie live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they both live with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you or your partner (if you have one) currently receiving Child Benefit for any of these children already, or has someone else claimed Child Benefit for them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody is currently claiming Child Benefit for any of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do any of your children have any special circumstances, such as being in hospital or care for extended periods, or do Alex and Charlie do any paid work of 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex is fostered - I'm fostering him - but I don't get anything from the council to foster him. Charlie and Alex don't work at all, they're only 7!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's very helpful information.

Let me now assess the eligibility for each of your three children based on what you've told me.

conversation.text:
## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility

Based on the information you've provided, here's the outcome for each of your children:

### ✅ **Alex (age 7) - ELIGIBLE**
You can claim Child Benefit for Alex. Since you're fostering him and the local council is not paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance, you qualify for Child Benefit under the fostering rules.

### ❌ **Blake (age 20) - INELIGIBLE**
Unfortunately, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Blake. He is 20 years old and working full-time, and is not in approved education or training. Child Benefit normally only continues past age 16 if the child is under 20 and in approved education or training.

### ✅ **Charlie (age 7) - ELIGIBLE**
You can claim Child Benefit for Charlie. He is under 16, lives with you in the UK, and meets all the standard eligibility criteria.

**Overall:** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for **2 out of your 3 children** - Alex and Charlie.

If you'd like to proceed with claiming, you can apply for Child Benefit for Alex and Charlie. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
